score:f7.notes: All four files present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection with 33 document entries, 45 excerpts, 7 prose blocks and 33 notes, queries.log) plus work/ (scripts and outputs) and docs/ (93 dumped documents). The run opened the vector artifacts (vec_check.py, vec1-4.py over semantic-vectors-index.json, the binary, the map and the 553 shards), so V1-V6 and V8 are scored. Verified against the read-only index copy: the coverage line, the 'soft power' zero, the positive control (14,090 in 77 of 77), the 202/143 pointed-at count, the frus1969-76v38p2 counts, and five quotation spot checks (all present in body_text, none apparatus); the digest pin holds across index, binary, map, shards manifest, all 553 shards and .generation; central-files-index.json maps 61D167 to 2198167 by control match. checks/ and the refuter/ folder (archival.py/.out) were written after the session and were not credited. The three violations: P6 (the log names archival1/3/4.out and a digest check whose outputs do not exist, and the memo claims every shell command is logged while the log lists its own elisions), V8 ('semantic vector files' in the overview's method paragraph) and O2' (five USIA entry numbers in the overview trace to no row, four of them absent from the memo entirely). Marginal calls recorded in the evidence: I3 treats the FTS5 content_rowid link as the virtual table's own mechanism rather than a table join; V1 credits a direct check of every shard over reading the shards manifest; V2 credits the segment round trip plus database lookups of every decoded neighbour in place of a named a-priori pair; E1 notes a 7-row leak of editorial-note citations in a 'whole volumes' pointed-at count; P5 treats the received 'about 56% precision elsewhere' as not the run's own share; O2 scores the quantities and leaves the identifiers to O2'.

refute:f7.fabricationDetails: None. (a) All 45 collection excerpts pass the segment-strict check (lower-case, [a-z0-9] only, segments in order at increasing offsets) against header||dateline||source_note||body_text of their own (volumeId, documentId); none contains an ellipsis, so each is one segment. (b) overview.md has no block quotes and 59 double-quoted spans. 38 are document quotations and every one is found, segment-strict, in the document the overview cites beside it: 'weak on propaganda' and 'are inclined by their psychology to wait and see who is winning' in frus1950v06/d32; 'not satisfactory' and 'USIE materials designed for world-wide or even area-wide distribution' in d15; 'stepped up to the limit of presently available funds' in d31; the Oriental-psychology sentence in d266; 'any feeling in the Oriental mind…' in frus1952-54v14p2/d551; 'mistaken in the oriental mind' in frus1952-54v13p2/d992; 'Not being Asians…' and 'the Oriental mind' in frus1958-60v01/d26; 'will make more difficult characterization of invasion as' in frus1952-54v12p1/d103; 'a fear of placing the U.S. in the position of appearing to support colonialism' in frus1955-57v22/d447; 'Asian minds' in d271; 'the most successful visit by an American, from a public image standpoint' in frus1917-72PubDipv06/d127; the three Tokyo 1968 spans and 'a strongly positive symbol' in frus1964-68v29p2/d123; 'Asians are, to varying degrees, America watchers' and 'usually depended more on the state of bi-lateral relations…' in frus1917-72PubDipv08/d31; 'We shall soon have nothing worthwhile left…' in frus1964-68v26/d106; the two 1967 spans in frus1917-72PubDipv07/d147; 'the lowest point in thirteen Saigon surveys' in d88; 'is now engaged in a massive campaign' in d129; 'cannot result primarily from American conceptions…' in d30; 'a long-range' in d146; 'a USIS audience' and 'reluctant to accept communist political and economic models' in d149; 'lack credibility', 'still see us as friends…' and 'very clearly in default' in frus1969-76v38p2/d105; 'has been effective', 'deeply implanted and persistent feeling' and 'withdrawing' in frus1977-80v30/d83; and the FRUS label 'S/P-NSC files, lot 61 D 167' in the source note of frus1952-54v12p2/d359. The remaining 21 spans are not document quotations and were excluded: the search terms 'soft power' (x3, one with a trailing full stop), 'public opinion poll', 'opinion survey', 'Department of State', 'prestige' (x2), 'image' (x2), 'propaganda' (x2) and 'effective'; the decision label 'policymakers'.'; the word 'lots'; the finding-aid titles 'Program Files' and 'Records Relating to the Voice of America'; the family term 'Oriental mind' in Finding 2's heading and twice in prose (it is nonetheless verbatim in d551, d60, d992 and d26); and the collection's title. Script: /Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/c3f/runs/f7/refuter/quotes.py, output quotes.out.

Findings against the session, in order of weight: V7 is violated on the task's definition, by labelling not concealment: the one document the memo lists as vector-only, frus1969-76v38p2/d105, is listed by the session's own header LIKE scan (scope5.out, re-run identical), the very scan the memo credits for d79/d81/d83; the practical claim (the vector step sent the session to that volume first) stands. The house-rules figure '11 of 695 bundled series' is presented as the session's own with no derivation, and the bundle in hand has 698 series (11 before 1940), so the figure was copied, not measured; '56% precision elsewhere' is attributed only to an unnamed 'elsewhere'. frus1955-57v22/d447 is in no saved document-listing output and no neighbour list; it matches the logged scoping MATCH predicates (so it counts as text-reached under 'test membership'), but the log does not show how it reached the screen, because cand.py's query strings were elided. The stated scope floor '1946' understates the documents' start (1945-11-01 in frus1946v08/v10). 'Record Group 305' is relayed as the editors printed it although the bundled record-group list has no RG 305 and the same note's FRC accession (306-84-0003) points to RG 306. The overview groups Carter 'National Security Affairs' and Ford 'National Security Adviser' series under 'National Security Council files'. The memo's wording 'documents in which officials use that wording' covers 32 hits several of which are Asian leaders' words relayed by officials (the memo's own classification says so). Minor: the memo says the map was used 'only to sample' yet reports an unclustered share against an era-matched baseline (labelled unreliable, nothing rests on it). No wrong number, no fabricated quotation and no mis-citation was found; the session's own checks (verify_quotes 45/0, check_overview, dump length equality) are real and I reproduced them.

vectorUse.notes: The memo treats neighbours as leads not evidence, prints raw cosine beside the calibrated score ((cos-0.40)/0.60, the index's documentOffset), excludes the editorial note frus1950v06/d9 from counts, reports 'no neighbour's volume absent from the index' (0 ABSENT_FROM_DB) and flags its near-duplicate cut (40 bits) as its own. v7.evidence: My strict re-run does not confirm the d105 claim: the session's own logged heading query returns it. queries.log: 'sqlite3 header LIKE scan of frus1969-76v38p2, frus1977-80v30 (Asia terms in header) -> work/scope5.out'; memo §2 step 5 gives the SQL (header LIKE '%Asia%' OR '%Japan%' OR … over frus1969-76v38p2, frus1977-80v30, frus1964-68v33, frus1969-76v02, apparatus excluded). work/scope5.out line 10: 'frus1969-76v38p2/d105|105. Memorandum From the Assistant Director for East Asia and the Pacific, United States Information Agency (Payeff) to the Director (Keogh) and Deputy Director (Kopp)|11622' - the header holds 'East Asia and the Pacific'. Re-run by me: 22 rows, identical to scope5.out, d105 among them (refuter/reach.out). d105 is further a member of the logged scope1 predicate ('"information agency" OR … OR propaganda', all volumes, the run's first scope step) and of the decade.py predicate over the 79 volumes, both run as count queries. The memo's sentence is literally true of document-listing MATCH queries (the family census does not match d105; cand.py excluded its volume) but fails the rule as set, which counts LIKE and heading queries: the memo credits that same header scan for d79, d81 and d83 and omits that it also lists d105. The violation is one of labelling, not concealment: the log order (vec2.py before the header scan) supports the memo's narrative that the vector step sent the session to the volume, which is why d105 is practically vector-reached.
